# AutoPoseSolver

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/AutoPoseSolver.cs#L94)

Closes each finger of a hand mesh onto whatever it is holding, stopping each one where it first
touches.

The travel runs between two fixed shapes: the hand's open pose and its closed one. Both ends
have to be fixed for the search to mean anything.

Never start from the player's tracked hand, however much better keeping their own shape
sounds. A grab fires *because* the player closed their hand, so the tracked fingers are
already most of the way shut and already through the object, and there is no travel left to
search.

Only the shape is solved. Where the hand *is* belongs to [`PhysicsHold`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHold),
which writes it once per step, and to the rule that a hand does not move against what it is
holding - so unlike the package this borrows its search from, nothing here relocates the palm.

Static and free of scene lookups on purpose: everything it needs is passed in, so it can be
driven outside play mode against a hand and a collider and the bends read back.

### Solve(HandSkeleton, IReadOnlyDictionary\<string, Quaternion>, HandPose, IReadOnlyList\<Collider>, AutoPoseSettings, List\<FingerSolve>) {#solve-handskeleton-quaternion-handpose-collider-autoposesettings-fingersolve}

Closes every finger onto the given colliders and leaves each where it first touches.

Works on any skeleton, so the grip an author sees on a ghost hand in the scene is solved by
the same code that will solve it at run time on the hand the player wears.

A finger of a worn hand is frozen once it is solved, so the tracking stops writing over it.
A hand with no solver behind it has nothing writing to it in the first place.
